To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DS was excessively toxic at high dose levels and ineffective at preventing the induction and persistence in the feline leukemia virus cat model.
DS is excessively toxic at doses that inhibit FeLV infection in vitro.
dextran sulfate by continuous intravenous administration is highly toxic at high doses in the feline leukemia virus disease model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of dextran sulfates as a treatment for HIV infection.
the development of antiviral agents for treatment and/or prophylaxis of retroviral infections.
the development of a novel antiviral drug, dextran sulfate, for the treatment of retrovirus-induced disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DS is ineffective in the treatment of feline leukemia and that the toxicity of the agent precludes its use in the treatment of AIDS.
dextran sulfate is not an effective antiviral agent in cats.
the FeLV cat is not an appropriate model for the study of the antiviral activity of DS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DS has no effect on FeLV replication in vitro, is highly toxic in vivo, and is ineffective in vivo in blocking FeLV infection.
DS is not an effective antiretroviral agent.
the FeLV model is not suitable for the study of DS antiviral activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the toxicity of the drug was not due to a specific effect on the immune system, as has been proposed for some other drugs, but to a general effect on the gastrointestinal mucosa.
the toxicity of DS is dose dependent and that the antiviral activity of DS in vitro does not predict antiviral activity in vivo.
the FeLV model is an excellent model for studying antiviral therapy.
